scalars.scalar_value: Bachelor’s degree and four (4) years full time or full time equivalent professional experience in the discipline; OR

items.item_text: 01. Equity Narrative: Please define what equity-mindedness means to you and provide a narrative that describes how your personal experiences in and/or outside the classroom enable you to put equity into practice to serve the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, ability, gender identities, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students and the community at large.
State Fire Training Fire Fighter I certification
State Fire Training Company Officer Certification
NFPA standards, ICS/NIMS protocols, and State Fire Training certification requirements.
State Fire Training Fire Fighter II certification AND
State Fire Training Lead Evaluator Certification (required within one year of employment)
Valid California driver’s license w/ Firefighter Endorsement or Commercial License to operate fire apparatus
State Fire Training Registered Instructor Certification (required within one year of employment)
NWCG Instructor Certification
Bachelor’s degree and four (4) years full time or full time equivalent professional experience in the discipline; OR
Associate’s degree and six (6) years full time or full time equivalent professional experience in the discipline AND
An incumbent must be insurable at the "standard rate" by the employer's insurance carrier at all times while employed in this classification by the College of the Sequoias.
Driving a vehicle to conduct work.
Fire suppression, prevention, and emergency response principles and techniques.
Hours will vary based on program needs
Federal, State and local laws, rules and regulations related to fire training, emergency medical services, and hazardous materials response.
Will require evenings and weekends during assigned academy hours
Principles of training and providing work direction.
Applicable laws, codes, regulations, policies and procedures related to State Fire Training (SFT) and the California Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM).
Operation of a computer and assigned software, including extensive use of Microsoft Office Suite and Adobe Professional and State Fire Training student management systems.
Coordinate complex instructional programs
Organize academy operations and logistics
Lead and collaborate with faculty and staff
Enforce fire training standards, academy rules and regulations.
Investigate and resolve student conduct and academy-related matters in accordance with established guidelines.
Train and provide work direction to others including but not limited to instructors, evaluators, company officers and class leadership.
Interpret, apply and explain rules, regulations, policies and procedures.
Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others.
Maintain and wear the approved uniform of the Fire Technology Coordinator.
Analyze situations accurately and adopt an effective course of action.
Meet schedules and timelines.
Work independently with little direction.
Plan and organize work.
Prepare comprehensive narrative and statistical reports.
Demonstrated sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students.
Indoor and outdoor work environment with ability to work some evening and weekend hours.
Knowledge of State Fire Training policies and procedures for ARTP instruction.
Effective communication skills, both oral and written.
Interpersonal skills using tact, patience and courtesy.
Diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students.
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
Operate a computer and assigned office equipment.
